category: X5-F1 Lightweight attack detection on embedded hardware
title: ARES: Adaptive robust object detection framework for enhancing real-time performance in autonomous vehicle systems
venue: Journal of Systems Architecture
key_idea: Run a fast low-security detector by default and switch to a costly certifiably robust detector only after a patch detector flags an attack, with schedulability analysis so detection tasks keep their deadlines.
method: Mixed-criticality style mode switch triggered by a patch detector, plus fixed-priority schedulability analysis and priority assignment for multi-camera detection tasks.
data: Randomly generated task sets for the schedulability study (per abstract); image data not named in the abstract
reported_result: Abstract: up to 8.9 times higher overall detection FPS than the baseline and 40.8 to 62.9 percent better acceptance ratio on random task sets.
relation_to_project: Supports the cheap-check-first shape shared by all five design slides: a detection flag gates an expensive defense. Baseline for the compute argument of contribution 5 and the latency budget of slide 05.
notes: Abstract assumes the certified detector defends once switched on; accuracy and false-alarm rate of the trigger detector and the hardware platform are not stated in the abstract (check full text).

category: X5-F1 Lightweight attack detection on embedded hardware
title: I Don't Know You, But I Can Catch You: Real-Time Defense against Diverse Adversarial Patches for Object Detectors
venue: Proceedings of the 2024 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
key_idea: NutNet: a small reconstruction autoencoder in front of the detector separates clean from patched image regions and masks suspected patches, covering hiding and appearing attacks with little added inference time.
method: Autoencoder-based patch detection on image regions followed by masking; six detectors (YOLOv2-v4, SSD, Faster R-CNN, DETR) in digital and physical tests.
data: INRIA Person; KITTI test images for the speed test (arXiv version)
reported_result: Abstract: inference time up 8 percent, clean performance down 0.4 percent, average defense 2.4 times (hiding) and 4.7 times (appearing) better than baselines. arXiv text: SAC roughly halves detection speed; ObjectSeeker needs seconds per image.
relation_to_project: Efficient patch-detection baseline for slide 01 and the overhead bar (about 8 percent) a cue-consistency checker must match. Detects patch statistics, not physical cue inconsistency.
code_or_data: sites.google.com/view/nutnet (demos, named in the abstract) UNVERIFIED
notes: Speed comparison numbers outside the abstract come from the arXiv HTML seen in a search snippet; GPU used for the FPS test not seen.

category: X5-F1 Lightweight attack detection on embedded hardware
title: LanCeX: A Versatile and Lightweight Defense Method against Condensed Adversarial Attacks in Image and Audio Recognition
venue: ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems
key_idea: Condensed (patch-like) perturbations cause abnormal activations that overwhelm semantic patterns; inference-inconsistency metrics flag such inputs at about one inference cost, followed by mitigation, aimed at embedded recognition.
method: Activation-inconsistency metrics inside the CNN for detection, then data recovery; applied to image classification, object detection and audio recognition.
reported_result: Abstract: average detection success 91, 85 and 90 percent for classification, object detection and audio; at most 3 times faster than compared defenses. Full-text copy seen in a search snippet: 521 ms versus more than 1813 ms for two other methods.
relation_to_project: Embedded-oriented patch detector that reports time cost; internal-activation alternative to the external appearance cue of slide 01; evidence for contribution 5.
notes: Crossref lists 2022 (online) and 2023 (issue). Precursor preprint LanCe (arXiv 1910.08536) covers image and audio only. Hardware behind the 521 ms figure not identified.

category: X5-F2 Compression and quantization effects on robustness and detection
title: Impact of Low-Bitwidth Quantization on the Adversarial Robustness for Embedded Neural Networks
venue: 2019 International Conference on Cyberworlds (CW)
key_idea: Low-bitwidth quantization is not a reliable defense: apparent robustness comes from gradient masking, while adversarial examples transfer poorly between full-precision and quantized models.
method: Evaluate binarized and low-bit quantized CNNs under gradient-based and gradient-free attacks and across bit-widths; explain poor transfer; sketch an ensemble defense.
data: CIFAR-10, SVHN (author slides seen in search)
reported_result: Abstract: quantization gives no robust protection and causes severe gradient masking; poor transferability explained by quantization value shift and gradient misalignment.
relation_to_project: If the laptop study quantizes the detector or the attack detector, apparent robustness may be gradient masking: evaluation needs gradient-free and transfer attacks (contributions 5 and 7).
notes: Image classification with digital perturbations only, not physical patches or detectors.

category: X5-F2 Compression and quantization effects on robustness and detection
title: Evaluating the Impact of Adversarial Patch Attacks on YOLO Models and the Implications for Edge AI Security
venue: International Journal of Information Security
key_idea: Naturalistic adversarial patches regenerated for recent Ultralytics YOLO versions evade person detection; smaller models chosen for edge latency were less robust than larger ones.
method: Port a naturalistic patch generator to YOLOv5, v8, v9 and v10; measure evasion; time inference on edge AI devices.
reported_result: Abstract: high evasion effectiveness on recent models; larger models more robust than smaller ones; smaller models respond faster on edge devices at higher attack risk.
relation_to_project: Evidence for the size-robustness trade-off behind contribution 5: the detector a vehicle can afford is the easier one to fool, so the checker should not rely on detector robustness.
code_or_data: Modified Ultralytics and patch-generation code on public GitHub repositories (stated in the article; links not recorded) UNVERIFIED
notes: Person detection, not traffic signs. Edge device models and timings not seen in the abstract.

category: X5-F2 Compression and quantization effects on robustness and detection
title: RobustMQ: benchmarking robustness of quantized models
venue: Visual Intelligence
key_idea: Benchmark of quantized ImageNet models under adversarial attacks, natural corruptions and systematic noise: quantized models resist attacks better but suffer more from corruptions and processing noise.
method: Systematic robustness evaluation of quantized versus floating-point models across bit-widths and noise types.
reported_result: Abstract: quantized models show higher adversarial but lower natural-corruption and systematic-noise robustness; more bits lowers adversarial and raises natural robustness; impulse noise and glass blur hurt most, brightness least.
relation_to_project: Predicts that a quantized pipeline reacts more to benign corruption (night noise, blur), which can raise false alarms of a consistency checker; argues for matched-false-alarm tests per bit-width (contributions 3 and 5).
notes: Classification only, digital attacks. The adversarial gain may partly reflect gradient masking (compare P2-P1404).

category: X5-F3 Latency and memory reporting practice in defense papers
title: Segment and Recover: Defending Object Detectors Against Adversarial Patch Attacks
venue: Journal of Imaging
key_idea: Training-free, patch-agnostic defense: localize large adversarial patches with an objectness-based frontend, then restore covered pixels by inpainting; reports a per-component runtime split.
method: Patch localization frontend plus LaMa inpainting backend in front of unchanged detectors (YOLOv11, Faster R-CNN, DETR).
data: ImageNet, Pascal VOC, INRIA, VisDrone-2019 (localization table seen in a search snippet)
reported_result: Full-text runtime table seen in a search snippet: patch localization under 1 ms, LaMa inpainting about 54 to 57 ms, base YOLOv11 32 to 69 ms per example.
relation_to_project: Shows flagging can cost under 1 ms while repair dominates the budget: supports a flag-and-explain design without repair (slide 01, contribution 5).
notes: Hardware for the runtime table not seen; the Small, Medium and Large labels of that table are not explained in the snippet.

category: X5-F2 Compression and quantization effects on robustness and detection
title: Spear: Evaluate the Adversarial Robustness of Compressed Neural Models
venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Third International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-24)
key_idea: Attacks that maximise the behaviour gap between a compressed model and its dense reference expose extra risk from sparsity and quantization, on classification and object detection.
method: Minimal-perturbation attack maximizing compressed-versus-dense output difference; tested on pruned (fine-grained, sparse tensor core) and INT8 QAT models.
data: RetinaNet and Mask R-CNN detectors (detection dataset not seen in the snippet)
reported_result: Full-text table seen in a search snippet: at epsilon 0.1 Spear lowers box AP of pruned and INT8 RetinaNet more than FGSM, DeepFool or PGD.
relation_to_project: Threat for deployment: an attacker who knows the vehicle runs a compressed detector can target the compression gap. A compressed-versus-reference disagreement check is a possible cue (contribution 5).
notes: Digital perturbations, not physical attacks.

category: X5-F1 Lightweight attack detection on embedded hardware
title: Can’t Slow Me Down: Learning Robust and Hardware-Adaptive Object Detectors against Latency Attacks for Edge Devices
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
key_idea: Latency attacks flood non-maximum suppression with phantom candidate boxes; background-attentive adversarial training tied to measured GPU capacity restores real-time detection on edge GPUs.
method: Profile NMS cost against GPU capacity, use objectness loss as a proxy, add background attention to adversarial training; YOLOv3, v5 and v8 on Jetson Xavier NX, Jetson Orin NX, RTX 4070 Ti Super and A100.
reported_result: Abstract: real-time processing restored from 13 FPS to 43 FPS on Jetson Orin NX with a better clean versus robust accuracy trade-off. arXiv text: latency back to 13, 17 and 23 ms for three YOLO generations on Orin NX.
relation_to_project: Attacks can target the time budget itself: a lightweight checker must report latency under attack, not only on clean frames (slide 05 p95 latency, contribution 5). Embedded GPU results for Q1.
notes: Defense is adversarial training, not a separate detector; the threat is an availability (latency) attack, not hiding or misclassification. Edge versus desktop bottleneck shift (compute-bound to memory-bound) described in the full text.

category: X5-F3 Latency and memory reporting practice in defense papers
title: Revisiting Adversarial Patch Defenses on Object Detectors: Unified Evaluation, Large-Scale Dataset, and New Insights
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
key_idea: Unified benchmark of 11 patch defenses for detectors that adds defense efficiency (milliseconds per image) and mask mIoU to AP and attack success rate; patch-detection accuracy proves a poor proxy for defense effect.
method: Re-evaluate defenses against 13 patch attacks on 11 detectors in digital, physical and adaptive settings; release a large patch dataset.
data: New patch dataset with 94 patch types and 94,000 images (abstract)
reported_result: Full-text table seen in a search snippet, time per image: SAC 44 ms, NAPGuard 59, Adyolo 62, NutNet 71, LGS 82, Jedi 349, Zmask 417, DIFFender 1240, PAD 32100 ms; NutNet best defense, SAC lowest cost.
relation_to_project: Closest reporting template for contribution 7 and the slide 01 baselines: mean ms per image is reported, but no tail latency, memory or energy was seen; a laptop study can add those.
notes: GPU behind the timing table not seen. Mean time only. Cross-task duplicate of P2-P1025 (LIT_X1), kept for the timing angle.

category: X5-F1 Lightweight attack detection on embedded hardware
title: Time-Constrained Adversarial Defense in IoT Edge Devices through Kernel Tensor Decomposition and Multi-DNN Scheduling
venue: Sensors
key_idea: eDenoizer lowers the latency of an adversarial denoiser on an edge device by Tucker-decomposing its convolution kernels and co-scheduling denoiser and protected model on a shared embedded GPU.
method: Tensor decomposition of denoiser kernels plus priority-aware multi-DNN scheduling that projects CPU-side priorities onto a priority-agnostic GPU.
reported_result: Abstract: classification accuracy drop at most 1.78 percent; inference speed with defense improved by up to 51.72 percent.
relation_to_project: Defense latency depends on GPU sharing with other DNNs, not only on model size: the laptop study should time the checker while the detector runs concurrently (slide 05, contribution 5).
notes: Denoiser for digital adversarial noise on classifiers, not physical attacks. Embedded board not named in the abstract.

category: X5-F1 Lightweight attack detection on embedded hardware
title: RobustEdge: Low Power Adversarial Detection for Cloud-Edge Systems
venue: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence
key_idea: A reduced-precision detector with early detection and exit runs on the edge device and blocks adversarial inputs before they reach the cloud classifier, saving transmission and detection energy.
method: Quantization-enabled energy separation training of 16-bit and 12-bit detectors; hardware evaluation on a 45 nm CMOS accelerator; Raspberry Pi energy comparison.
reported_result: arXiv abstract: 16-bit and 12-bit detectors reach AUC above 0.9; 25 times lower detection energy than prior work on the 45 nm accelerator; more than 166 times better system energy efficiency than cloud-side detection.
relation_to_project: Evidence that a reduced-precision attack detector can keep detection quality, and one of few papers reporting energy (Q1 and Q2; contribution 5).
notes: Digital gradient and score-based attacks on classifiers, not physical attacks. Numbers from the arXiv abstract; the journal version may differ.

category: X5-F1 Lightweight attack detection on embedded hardware
title: WIP: A First Look At Employing Large Multimodal Models Against Autonomous Vehicle Attacks
venue: Proceedings Symposium on Vehicle Security & Privacy (VehicleSec 2024)
key_idea: A large multimodal model serves as a verification layer for traffic signs and is activated only when the vehicle is within about 7 m of a detected sign, to judge whether the sign is adversarial.
method: Continuous sign detection and classification; GPT-4V queried on frames near the sign; tests with a stereo camera viewing attack images shown on a TV screen.
data: NDD attack examples (as named in the paper); ZED X stereo camera with a ZED Box
reported_result: Full-text snippet: adversarial-sign identification by the LMM was reliable up to 7 m and dropped beyond it, so 7 m became the activation range.
relation_to_project: Distance-gated activation of a heavy verifier; contrast for contribution 5: a cheap cue check can run every frame where an LMM cannot. Supports the abstain idea when evidence is too weak at range.
notes: Work-in-progress workshop paper. Details from the full text seen in a web search snippet, no abstract record read. Where the LMM runs and its latency were not seen. A related IV 2024 paper by the same first author (DOI 10.1109/iv55156.2024.10588595) was seen in Crossref, not read.

category: X5-F1 Lightweight attack detection on embedded hardware
title: Attention-Based Real-Time Defenses for Physical Adversarial Attacks in Vision Applications
venue: 2024 ACM/IEEE 15th International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems (ICCPS)
key_idea: Physical adversarial objects over-activate a few channels in shallow layers; tracing those channels across video frames lets a defense detect and mask attacks with one inference pass per frame instead of two.
method: Adversarial-Channel Attention Tracing (ACAT): a single-frame defense initializes the attack mask; channel attention on shallow layers then tracks the adversarial trace frame by frame.
data: Real-time segmentation models DDRNet-Slim23 and BiSeNetX39; LGS among the baselines (full-text snippet)
reported_result: Full-text snippet: better defense than compared single-frame methods at lower total inference time; timing close to LGS, which defends poorly against physical attacks (figure values not recorded).
relation_to_project: Closest low-cost multi-frame mechanism to slide 05 (bounded frame memory) and an internal-activation contrast to the external cues of slides 01 to 04. Threatens a claim that cheap temporal carrying of evidence is new.
notes: Semantic segmentation, not object detection. Timing hardware not seen. Content from full-text passages seen in web search snippets. Cross-task duplicate of P2-P508 (LIT_A5); kept for the timing angle.

category: X5-F1 Lightweight attack detection on embedded hardware
title: Model Agnostic Defense against Adversarial Patch Attacks on Object Detection in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
venue: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
key_idea: A tiny single-stage model of about 1.2 million parameters handles adversarial patches in front of an unchanged UAV object detector and is sized for onboard deployment.
method: Train a small patch-handling model on VisDrone; compare with segmentation-based patch masking; digital and physical tests; measure added processing time.
reported_result: Full-text snippet: about 4 percent added processing time per image, without quantization or other optimization.
relation_to_project: Size and overhead reference for the tiny head of slide 01 and contribution 5: an embedded-size patch model is feasible.
notes: UAV vehicle detection, not road scenes or signs. Hardware for the timing not seen. Content from full-text passages seen in web search snippets.

category: X5-F3 Latency and memory reporting practice in defense papers
title: Defending Person Detection Against Adversarial Patch Attack by Using Universal Defensive Frame
venue: IEEE Transactions on Image Processing
key_idea: A universal defensive frame, optimized in competition with adversarial patches, is attached around the input image to protect person detection at very small added computation.
method: Iterative competing optimization of patch and defensive frame; the frame is applied at inference in front of YOLO-v2 and Faster R-CNN.
data: INRIA Person and a collected dataset (full-text snippet)
reported_result: Full-text snippet: on a GTX 1080 Ti, time per image rose from 23.1 to 28.3 ms for YOLO-v2 and from 70.0 to 83.1 ms for Faster R-CNN.
relation_to_project: Example of reporting the defense's own runtime per detector on a named GPU; near-zero-cost input-side baseline (contribution 5, Q1).
notes: Person detection; mean time only. Content from full-text passages seen in web search snippets.

category: X5-F2 Compression and quantization effects on robustness and detection
title: Noise Sensitivity-Based Energy Efficient and Robust Adversary Detection in Neural Networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
key_idea: A layer-wise adversarial noise sensitivity metric picks where to attach a small binary detector; the quantized network plus detector stops adversarial inputs early and is priced in energy on scalable hardware.
method: Noise-sensitivity layer selection, small neural detector, quantization of weights and activations, MAC and memory-access energy analysis with early exit.
data: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 with VGG19 and ResNet18 (full-text snippet)
reported_result: Full-text snippet: detector AUC reported against weight and activation bit precision; for 12-bit ResNet18 with early exit, MAC energy is 1.01 times baseline with no adversarial inputs and 0.32 times with 99 percent adversarial inputs.
relation_to_project: Only row that tracks a detector-of-attack against bit precision (Q2) and prices the detector in energy (Q1).
notes: Digital attacks on classifiers. The snippet does not show the direction of the AUC change at lower precision. Content from full-text passages seen in web search snippets.

category: X5-F2 Compression and quantization effects on robustness and detection
title: Relationship between Model Compression and Adversarial Robustness: A Review of Current Evidence
venue: 2023 IEEE Symposium Series on Computational Intelligence (SSCI)
key_idea: Review of studies on quantization, pruning and adversarial robustness: naive compression can reduce robustness, moderate pruning can preserve it, and past a critical compression ratio robustness falls before accuracy.
method: Literature review comparing reported experiments on quantization, pruning and adversarial training.
reported_result: Conclusion snippet: naive pruning and quantization can reduce robustness; within limits pruning may preserve or improve it; beyond a critical ratio first robustness, then accuracy decrease.
relation_to_project: Summary answer to Q2 and a caution for contribution 5: compress the detector only with robustness measured at each step.
notes: Mostly classifier studies. Content from the conclusion seen in a web search snippet.

category: X5-F3 Latency and memory reporting practice in defense papers
title: Practitioner Paper: A Real-Time Defense Against Object Vanishing Adversarial Patch Attacks for Object Detection in Autonomous Vehicles
venue: Lecture Notes of the Institute for Computer Sciences, Social Informatics and Telecommunications Engineering (LNICST)
key_idea: ADAV flags frames whose detections disagree with preceding frames, then localizes and masks the patch; latency is measured separately for clean and attacked frames because the two paths differ.
method: Two-stage defense: frame-level attack detection from prior-frame consistency, then patch localization and masking; LGS, JPEG and a universal defense frame as baselines.
data: 100 BDD100K videos plus 100 synthetic adversarial versions, 240,000 frames (133 minutes)
reported_result: arXiv snippet: attack detection recall 0.95 for patch scale above 0.8 and 0.52 below; on a T4 GPU 56 FPS clean and 20 FPS attacked versus 63 FPS undefended; adversarial mAP 0.36 versus 0.22 undefended.
relation_to_project: Named on slide 05 as the baseline; this row records its timing practice (separate clean and attacked FPS), which the owner's comparison should match.
notes: Cross-task duplicate of P2-P501 (LIT_A5), kept for the timing angle. The published title carries the prefix Practitioner Paper; the conference behind the LNICST volume not seen. Content from the arXiv HTML seen in web search snippets.

category: X5-F2 Compression and quantization effects on robustness and detection
title: Quantization Robustness to Input Degradations for Object Detection
venue: 2025 Innovations in Intelligent Systems and Applications Conference (ASYU)
key_idea: Post-training quantization of YOLO detectors (FP32, FP16, dynamic UINT8, static INT8) tested under noise, blur, low contrast and JPEG degradations, with a degradation-aware INT8 calibration.
method: Five YOLO12 scales converted with TensorRT and ONNX Runtime; COCO val2017 with synthetic degradations; RTX 2070 GPU.
data: COCO val2017 with synthetic degradations; INT8 calibration on 1000 COCO train2017 images
reported_result: arXiv abstract and snippet: static INT8 gives significant speedups; mixed clean and degraded calibration did not consistently improve robustness over clean calibration, except possibly against noise in larger models.
relation_to_project: Deployment recipe and benign-degradation baseline for an INT8 detector on a laptop-class GPU; informs whether quantization changes hard-negative behaviour at night (contributions 3 and 5).
notes: Benign degradations only, no adversarial attacks.

category: X5-F2 Compression and quantization effects on robustness and detection
title: Robustness in Compressed Neural Networks for Object Detection
venue: 2021 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
key_idea: Pruned object detectors on autonomous-driving data: clean accuracy hides the cost of compression; sensitivity to synthetic distortions varies strongly by distortion type, and some classes lose far more than others.
method: Structured and unstructured pruning of detectors; texture-invariant augmentation; tests under synthetic distortions and per-class accuracy; class-balancing remedies.
data: Autonomous driving datasets (names not seen in the snippet)
reported_result: Snippet of the arXiv HTML: compressed models' sensitivity differed widely between distortion types, some barely affected; compression hit classes unevenly; class balancing raised mAP, most for structured pruning at high compression.
relation_to_project: Benign-side evidence for Q2: after compression, false alarms and misses of a consistency checker must be measured per class and per condition, not only on clean averages (contributions 3 and 5).
notes: Benign distortions, no adversarial attacks. arXiv id taken from a search result address and not checked in this run (shared arXiv stop); the row is verified through its DOI.

category: X5-F2 Compression and quantization effects on robustness and detection
title: Defensive Quantization: When Efficiency Meets Robustness
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR)
key_idea: Conventional quantization keeps clean accuracy but loses much more accuracy under adversarial attack than full precision; a quantization method designed jointly for efficiency and robustness is proposed.
method: Empirical study of quantized VGG-16 and Wide ResNet under FGSM on CIFAR-10, then a robustness-aware quantization scheme.
data: CIFAR-10 (figure caption seen in the arXiv PDF snippet)
reported_result: Snippet of the arXiv PDF: quantized models lose no clean accuracy down to 4 to 5 bits but lose markedly more accuracy under FGSM than full-precision models.
relation_to_project: Counterpoint to P2-P1406 for Q2: naive quantization of the detector can make attacks easier, so the deployed precision must be the one attacked and evaluated (contribution 5).
notes: Venue from the header of the arXiv PDF (published as a conference paper at ICLR 2019) seen in a search snippet; no DOI. Classification with digital attacks only. arXiv record not checked in this run (shared arXiv stop in force): NEEDS_VERIFY.
